title: d'Yvoy's cipher despatches and the Hereditary Prince's letters to him, London-Berlin 1797-99 (KHA A35-1450-1453)

documents.route: M.L. d'Yvoy (London, Hampton Court) <-> Hereditary Prince (Berlin, Schonhausen)

plaintext.source: Contemporary Dutch decipherment written over most code runs.

transcription.source: KHA renditions (original size): runs_a.txt to runs_d.txt
transcription.notes: Measured file runs_a.txt holds context, CT, PT and AL lines. Several outgoing letters survive only as mirror-image tissue copies.

documents.shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, A35 Willem I, inv. A35-1452, A35-1453

plaintext.source: Interlinear decipherments; several 1799 letters printed in Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken III.

system.summary: Dutch word code of 1-4 digit numbers (up to about 1,500) for words, names and places, plus syllable numbers for spelling; two different tables, London 1797-98 and 1799.
system.notes: A stock phrase 'hier achter is (wat) geschreven' points to sympathetic-ink text on the back.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherments; Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken III (1906-07) prints d'Yvoy letters of 1799

conditions.human_role: Lead chosen by the user from the KHA sweep; user asked to rebuild the code from the glosses and read the unglossed letters.
tools: tables.py vote tables with leave-one-page-out test

solution.what: Colenbrander Gedenkstukken II and III downloaded in full text and searched: d'Yvoy letters of 1795-96 (GS II) and 1799 (GS III) printed; none of 1797-98.
28 flagged pages transcribed with glosses (runs_a, runs_b); all runs glossed.
Second pass over all 1,029 scans of A35-1450-1453: 196 pages with code numbers listed (more_pages.tsv).
79 pages marked unglossed transcribed (runs_c, runs_d); many glossed after all.
Two code tables voted from the glossed runs (L 102 numbers, E 50); leave-one-page-out: L 79% vs 26%, E 81% vs 27%.

Unglossed runs decoded: nearly all are the stock pointer 'hier achter is (wat) geschreven' (229 = achter), read from glossed instances; 147107 (mirror copy of No. 22, 22 Sept 1797) only about 40% decoded.
No. 22's mounted original found at 147106 beside its tissue copy 147107; all twelve runs carry the Dutch decipherment; transcribed (runs_e.txt) and added to table L (105 numbers, 78% vs 26%).
Colenbrander GS III no. 691 (11 May 1799) compared with cipher page 147442: the print is the sympathetic-ink text, the cipher only the pointer phrase; the 1799 prints cannot extend table E.

outcome.method_basis: Every code run carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment (read from the originals), except a recurring pointer phrase read from its glossed instances; the two code tables were rebuilt from the glosses (leave-one-page-out 78% and 81%).
outcome.notes: Two distinct codes (London 1797-98, 1799). No. 22 (22 Sept 1797) read from its mounted original 147106.

credits.note: interlinear Dutch decipherments written over the code runs in the Hereditary Prince's household and by d'Yvoy

texts.label: No. 22, the Hereditary Prince to d'Yvoy, Schonhausen 22 Sept 1797 (147106)
texts.summary: The Prince thanks d'Yvoy for his letters Nos. 47-48 and his handling of a conversation with His Royal Highness; Tollius is satisfied with his first conferences with Their Highnesses; the Prince cannot act until he has an answer to letters sent by Kiehl, which may bring a change in d'Yvoy's position at Hampton Court; the effect of 18 Fructidor on the Lille and Udine negotiations. Code runs from the contemporary Dutch interlinear decipherment.

reading_review.note: The code runs of No. 22 read from the contemporary Dutch decipherment on the mounted original 147106 (one word, run 2, uncertain); with the clear French they make continuous sentences, translated in reading_no22_en.md. Some clear French words illegible on the scan are marked. Not checked by a human against the image.

texts.label: The Hereditary Prince to d'Yvoy, Schonhausen 7 June 1799 (147481), run by run
texts.summary: Clear French with Dutch code runs on the garrisons of Holland, Zeeland, Nijmegen and 's-Hertogenbosch, Tuyll, Grenville and the Hereditary Prince, each run with its contemporary Dutch decipherment (PT lines).

reading_review.note: Each code run with its contemporary Dutch decipherment inside the transcribed clear context (about eight words either side); the runs read as Dutch phrases fitting the French around them (Tuyll's return journey, South Prussia, the lapsed correspondence with Prussia). Not a continuous text; three gloss words uncertain (Inghuyzen, Gepa.., cortte). Not checked by a human against the image.
